text: Root-path versions; u + v − lca − parent(lca).

Persistent segment trees on a tree (树上主席树): give every vertex the value tree of its whole root path, built from its parent's version plus its own value (进阶篇第8章 did the same along an array). Then the multiset of values on the path u–v is version(u) + version(v) − version(lca) − version(parent(lca)), and the k-th smallest is found by walking those four trees together (Count on a tree, P2633).
Memory n log n nodes; each query O(log n) after an LCA. Forests that merge (森林 P3302) rebuild the smaller tree's versions on top of the other one (small-to-large).

Random tree and path queries, checked against listing the path's values and sorting them in Python. Subtracting version(lca) and version(parent(lca)) removes the shared root part but keeps the LCA itself exactly once.
Max, strict second max, count; amortised chmin.

Segment tree beats (吉司机线段树) supports the "range chmin" update ai = min(ai, x) together with range sums. Each node stores the maximum mx, the strict second maximum se, and how many times the maximum occurs, cnt. For an update with x: if x ≥ mx, nothing changes; if se < x < mx, only the maximums change, so sum −= cnt·(mx − x) and mx = x right here (a lazy tag); otherwise recurse into the children.

The "otherwise" case looks slow, but it merges the two largest distinct values of the node, which can only happen O(log n) times per value: amortised O((n + q) log n) for chmin with sums. Historic maxima (CPU 监控 P4314, P6242) add more tags on the same idea.
Random chmin, sum and max operations checked against a plain array in Python. The push uses the parent's mx as a "chmin tag": a child can only be above it in its maximum.
Deepest child; shifted arrays; O(n) merges.

Long-path decomposition (长链剖分): like heavy-light, but the "long" child is the one with the deepest subtree. For DP indexed by depth (f[u][j] = number of vertices j levels below u), the long child's array can be reused by shifting it one place (f[u][j + 1] = f[long][j]) with a shared memory pool, and only short children are merged element by element.

Every vertex is the top of exactly one long chain, and a short child's array has length = its chain length, so all merges together cost O(n). Uses: depth-indexed tree DP (CF1009F Dominant Indices), k-th ancestor in O(1) after O(n log n) preprocessing (P5903).

For every vertex: the smallest depth j (below it) with the most vertices at that depth in its subtree. Checked in Python by walking each subtree layer by layer.

Ties matter: when the long child's best depth ties with a smaller depth, the smaller one must win. Here a full tie (every depth has one vertex) resets the answer to 0, and short-chain merges prefer smaller j on equal counts.
dist; merge down right spines; delete-min with DSU.

A leftist heap (左偏树 , a mergeable heap 可并堆) is a binary heap-ordered tree where each node stores dist = length of the shortest path down to a missing child. The rule dist(left) ≥ dist(right) keeps the right spine O(log n) long, so two heaps merge in O(log n) by walking down right spines: keep the smaller root, merge its right child with the other heap, swap children if the rule breaks.

Push = merge with a one-node heap; pop = merge the two children of the root. Together with a DSU that maps each element to its heap root this solves "merge the heaps of x and y / delete the minimum of x's heap" (P3377). Its persistent version (copy nodes on the merge path) gives the fast k-th shortest path algorithm (NOI 篇第11章).

Random merges and delete-mins (ties broken by the smaller index, as in P3377), checked against plain Python sets. The deleted root keeps pointing to the new root, so path compression still finds the right heap for every element.
Binarise; split at the most balanced edge.

Edge divide and conquer (边分治): like centroid decomposition (点分治), but split the tree at the edge whose removal leaves the most balanced two parts. Every path through that edge is "a path in the left part ending at its end + the edge + a path in the right part", so each step combines exactly two sides, which is easier than merging many subtrees of a centroid.

A star breaks it (every edge leaves a part of size n − 1), so first binarise the tree: replace each vertex's children by a chain of virtual vertices joined by weight-0 edges. Degrees become ≤ 3 and the best edge always leaves parts of size ≥ about n/3, so the depth is O(log n). Virtual vertices are not counted. Used when the two-sided merge matters (P4220 通道 , and many "maximise f(path) over pairs" problems).

Key points to memorise
1. Tree chairman: version(u) = version(parent) + a[u]; path = u + v − lca − fa(lca).
2. Beats node: max, strict second max, count of max, sum.
3. chmin x: x ≥ max ⇒ stop; se < x < max ⇒ tag here; else recurse.
4. Long-path: child with the deepest subtree; reuse its array shifted by one.
5. Merging short chains costs their lengths: O(n) total.
6. Leftist heap: dist(left) ≥ dist(right); merge along right spines, O(log n).
7. Edge D&C: binarise (degree ≤ 3), cut the balanced edge, merge exactly two sides.
